title: Backups: restore your work and prove independence
goal: Dump a DT, restore only into a new base and compare two requests before and after changing the copy.
prerequisites: 1c-enterprise.a 5; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.
outcomes: Distinguish CF configuration from DT state backup.
Open the restored base and compare identities/values.
Change the copy while preserving the source’s 75 minutes.
sections: A configuration export describes the solution but is not a full copy of customer documents. An infobase dump preserves data with configuration in its supported format. Copying an open file directory can be inconsistent. Choose a supported method and ensure the required absence of active writes.

Create own customer/service Контроль A6 and two requests of 30 and 45 minutes. Record actual codes, numbers, dates, statuses and the 75-minute control. Retain earlier work; the entire-base total may exceed 75. CF represents configuration; a DT is used to transfer infobase state including data.
A file is not a verified restore

Creating a backup file does not prove usability. Restore it into a fresh empty directory, open it and reconcile identities, count, totals and configuration version. File size or extension alone cannot detect the wrong source or a logically incomplete copy.

Close Enterprise and use Designer’s normal infobase dump into a new DT. Record path, time and versions. Copying an actively modified 1CD is not a substitute for this checked route. File existence alone does not establish recovery: opening a separate restored target is required.
The source is never the target

Record source and fresh destination paths before the operation. If the destination exists, choose another; never erase it automatically. After restore, change the copy to 90 minutes and reread the 75-minute source. This proves independent working instances rather than two shortcuts to one infobase.

Create a new empty infobase without configuration using a new name and directory. Restore replaces the selected target’s contents, so verify its actual path and absence of work first. Never test a dangerous overwrite on your only source; stop such a case before execution.

A damaged or unsuitable file should produce explicit rejection. Do not repair the only backup in place or test it by overwriting work. Preserve a file copy, a safe error classification and unchanged source. A recovery plan also identifies storage, acceptable loss of recent changes and responsibility for verification.

Verify both restored requests and 75, then change only the first copy request from 30 to 45. Its set becomes 90; the source must retain 30/45 and 75. Two list entries pointing to one directory are not independent copies. If verification fails, retain the DT and both states for diagnosis rather than overwrite the only archive.

lab.title: Source 75, separate restored copy 90
lab.environment: Own original service desk; synthetic records only. No real Nexus accounts, Windows identities or external services are changed.

Choose no configuration, a new teaching name and a new empty directory. Compare its path with the source before opening target Designer.
Recheck empty-target name/path, choose your DT and confirm replacement of only that target. Wait for completion and open its Enterprise.

Allowed/refused cases, completed controls and explicit untested scope; no secrets.
lab.negative: Use the second worked case to identify the unsafe or unproved condition. Never perform destructive restoration over existing work.
